"'''The Only Way Is Up'''" is a song written by [[George Jackson (songwriter)|George Jackson]] and Johnny Henderson and originally released in 1980 as a single by American soul singer [[Otis Clay]]. In 1988, it became a chart-topping single in the United Kingdom for [[Yazz|Yazz and the Plastic Population]].

"The Only Way Is Up" is a song written by George Jackson and Johnny Henderson and originally released in 1980 as a single by American soul singer Otis Clay. In 1988, it became a chart-topping single in the United Kingdom for Yazz and the Plastic Population.

sections.heading: Otis Clay version
sections.wikitext: The song was written by [[George Jackson (songwriter)|George Jackson]] and Johnny Henderson.<ref>{{cite book |first=Felicia Kate |last=Solomon |year=2019 |chapter=Musical Acknowledgments |chapter-url=https://books.google.com/books?id=gsiCDwAAQBAJ&pg=PA516 |title=Lucia's Poltergeist |page=516 |publisher=Troubador Publishing |location=[[Leicestershire]] |isbn=978-1789015-799 }}</ref> It was first recorded by Otis Clay and released as a single by Echo Records in 1980.<ref>[https://www.northernsouldirect.co.uk/shop/7-vinyl/otis-clay-the-only-way-is-up-messing-with-my-mind-demo-45-outta-sight-7-vinyl/  "Otis Clay – The Only Way Is Up / Messing With My Mind ", ''Northern Soul Direct'']. Retrieved December 3, 2020</ref> Though not a hit, the song became the title track of Clay's album ''The Only Way Is Up'',<ref>[https://books.google.com/books?id=BwwLBaH9488C&dq=%22Otis+Clay%22+%22only+way+is+up%22+soul&pg=PT877  Jon Kutner, Spencer Leigh (eds.), ''1,000 UK Number One Hits'', Omnibus Press, 2010, p.]</ref> released in Japan in 1982 and then North America in 1985.<ref>{{cite news |first=Greg |last=Barr |date=September 23, 1988 |url=https://www.proquest.com/docview/239260543 |title=Feats of Clay |url-access=registration |work=The Ottawa Citizen |page=B3 |issn=0839-3222 |publisher=Postmedia Network |access-date=December 3, 2020 |id={{ProQuest|239260543}} }}</ref> It is also included on his 2012 album ''Truth Is''.<ref>{{cite interview |first=Otis |last=Clay |title=Q&A: Singer Otis Clay's got the blues and more |url=https://www.proquest.com/docview/1527024501 |interviewer-first=Kevin C |interviewer-last=Johnson |work=TCA Regional News |publisher=Tribune Content Agency |date=May 22, 2014 |url-access=registration |access-date=December 3, 2020 }}</ref>
sections.text: The song was written by George Jackson and Johnny Henderson. It was first recorded by Otis Clay and released as a single by Echo Records in 1980. Though not a hit, the song became the title track of Clay's album The Only Way Is Up, released in Japan in 1982 and then North America in 1985. It is also included on his 2012 album Truth Is.

The Yazz version was produced by [[Jonathan More]] and [[Matt Black (DJ)|Matt Black]] (better known as dance duo [[Coldcut]], who had worked with British singer Yazz on their hit single "[[Doctorin' the House]]"). "The Only Way Is Up" was Yazz's first solo single, credited to her under the name Yazz and the Plastic Population. Released in July 1988 by [[Big Life]] as the first single from her debut album, ''[[Wanted (Yazz album)|Wanted]]'' (1988), the song became an instant smash hit, spending five weeks at the top of the [[UK Singles Chart]], and ultimately becoming Britain's second biggest-selling single of 1988. Also on the [[Eurochart Hot 100]], it soared to the number one position. In the United States it reached number two on the [[Hot Dance Club Songs|''Billboard'' dance chart]], although only making number 96 on the [[Billboard Hot 100|''Billboard'' Hot 100]].<ref>{{cite book |title= Hot Dance/Disco: 1974-2003|last=Whitburn |first=Joel |author-link=Joel Whitburn |year=2004 |publisher=Record Research |page=285}}</ref>

A 2009 remix was released in the United Kingdom on September 7, 2009.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.radio1.gr/music/forthcoming_uk_singles.htm |title=Radio1 Rodos :: New Music :: U.K. Forthcoming Releases |publisher=Radio1.gr |access-date=March 20, 2014}}</ref>

The Yazz version was produced by Jonathan More and Matt Black (better known as dance duo Coldcut, who had worked with British singer Yazz on their hit single "Doctorin' the House"). "The Only Way Is Up" was Yazz's first solo single, credited to her under the name Yazz and the Plastic Population. Released in July 1988 by Big Life as the first single from her debut album, Wanted (1988), the song became an instant smash hit, spending five weeks at the top of the UK Singles Chart, and ultimately becoming Britain's second biggest-selling single of 1988. Also on the Eurochart Hot 100, it soared to the number one position. In the United States it reached number two on the Billboard dance chart, although only making number 96 on the Billboard Hot 100.

A 2009 remix was released in the United Kingdom on September 7, 2009.

sections.heading: Background and release
sections.wikitext:
After leaving school, Yazz got a job in a nightclub in Soho and got into her first band called The Biz. She also worked as a model and then met the managers of [[Wham!]] who would be her managers. She took singing lessons and made demo songs that was introduced to electronic music duo [[Coldcut]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.crossrhythms.co.uk/articles/music/Yazz_The_only_way_is_up_for_the_singer_who_is_now_a_powerful_woman_of_God/30570/p1/|title=Yazz: The only way is up for the singer who is now a powerful woman of God|publisher=crossrhythms.co.uk|access-date=September 4, 2017}}</ref> Together, they wrote "[[Doctorin' the House]]" which incorporates [[sampling (music)|samples]] from various sources, mainly TV and film dialogue. It reached number six on the [[UK Singles Chart]] in March 1988 and was a club staple. The next song they would release was "The Only Way Is Up". 

Yazz told in a 1988 interview, "It was first suggested that Coldcut do a remake of the track. But they weren't keen because they felt they might spoil the original, but I felt it would be perfect for me." Coldcut decided, however, to take on the production role. Yazz expanded, "It was a real challenge for them to work with a live vocalist, as well as for me for my first single. With "Doctorin' the House" they had laid down the groove and then said 'OK, now sing over it.' This time the song was arranged and structured before we even started recording."<ref>{{cite magazine|first=Tim|last=Jeffery|url=https://www.flickr.com/photos/57779449@N02/49137306056/in/album-72157711976935893/|title=''RM'' Dance|magazine=[[Record Mirror]]|date=July 16, 1988|page=18|access-date=March 12, 2023}}</ref> Their [[House music|house]] version of "The Only Way Is Up" was released in July 1988, and become a huge hit in the clubs and on the charts.
sections.text:
After leaving school, Yazz got a job in a nightclub in Soho and got into her first band called The Biz. She also worked as a model and then met the managers of Wham! who would be her managers. She took singing lessons and made demo songs that was introduced to electronic music duo Coldcut. Together, they wrote "Doctorin' the House" which incorporates samples from various sources, mainly TV and film dialogue. It reached number six on the UK Singles Chart in March 1988 and was a club staple. The next song they would release was "The Only Way Is Up". 

Yazz told in a 1988 interview, "It was first suggested that Coldcut do a remake of the track. But they weren't keen because they felt they might spoil the original, but I felt it would be perfect for me." Coldcut decided, however, to take on the production role. Yazz expanded, "It was a real challenge for them to work with a live vocalist, as well as for me for my first single. With "Doctorin' the House" they had laid down the groove and then said 'OK, now sing over it.' This time the song was arranged and structured before we even started recording." Their house version of "The Only Way Is Up" was released in July 1988, and become a huge hit in the clubs and on the charts.

sections.heading: Critical reception
sections.wikitext: Bill Coleman from ''[[Billboard (magazine)|Billboard]]'' magazine named the song a "annoyingly catchy [[Dance-pop|disco/pop]] smash".<ref>{{cite magazine|first=Bill|last=Coleman|url=https://www.worldradiohistory.com/hd2/IDX-Business/Music/Billboard-Index/IDX/1988/1988-12-03-Billboard-Page-0025.pdf|title=Yazz Is 'Wanted' For Assault With A Catchy Beat|magazine=[[Billboard (magazine)|Billboard]]|date=December 3, 1988|page=27|access-date=June 13, 2024}}</ref> Pan-European magazine ''[[Music & Media]]'' wrote, "Produced by [[Coldcut]], this is an electro-soul number with more than a touch of [[House music|house]] influences. A good, radio-friendly, dance song."<ref>{{cite magazine|first=|last=|url=https://worldradiohistory.com/UK/Music-and-Media/80s/1988/M&M-1988-08-06.pdf|title=Previews: Singles|magazine=[[Music & Media]]|volume=5|issue=32|date=August 6, 1988|page=15|accessdate=July 20, 2022}}</ref> Matthew Collin from ''[[Record Mirror]]'' declared it as "a tale of love under stress, dedication and survival, all set to an infectious house beat." He added, "'The Only Way Is Up' is where bad house music crashes into gay Seventies disco and ends up in the top 10."<ref>{{cite magazine|first=Matthew|last=Collin|url=https://www.flickr.com/photos/57779449@N02/49137431491/in/album-72157711975737862/|title=''RM'' Dance|magazine=[[Record Mirror]]|date=July 23, 1988|page=20|access-date=March 12, 2023}}</ref> In 2025, ''[[Classic Pop]]'' ranked it number six in their list of "Top 20 Cover Versions of the 80s".<ref>{{cite magazine|first=Jon|last=O'Brien|url=https://www.classicpopmag.com/top-songs/top-20-cover-versions-80s/|title=Top 20 cover versions of the 80s|magazine=[[Classic Pop]]|date=April 22, 2025|access-date=June 23, 2025}}</ref>
sections.text: Bill Coleman from Billboard magazine named the song a "annoyingly catchy disco/pop smash". Pan-European magazine Music & Media wrote, "Produced by Coldcut, this is an electro-soul number with more than a touch of house influences. A good, radio-friendly, dance song." Matthew Collin from Record Mirror declared it as "a tale of love under stress, dedication and survival, all set to an infectious house beat." He added, "'The Only Way Is Up' is where bad house music crashes into gay Seventies disco and ends up in the top 10." In 2025, Classic Pop ranked it number six in their list of "Top 20 Cover Versions of the 80s".

sections.heading: Chart performance
sections.wikitext:
Yazz' cover of "The Only Way Is Up" was very successful globally. In Europe, it peaked at number-one in Belgium, Denmark, Ireland, Luxembourg, the Netherlands, Sweden
and the United Kingdom. In the last of these, it hit the top spot in its third week at the [[UK Singles Chart]], on July 31, 1988.<ref>{{cite web|title=Official Singles Chart Top 100 31 July 1988 - 06 August 1988|url=https://www.officialcharts.com/charts/singles-chart/19880731/7501/|publisher=[[Official Charts Company]]|access-date=September 17, 2020}}</ref> The single spent a total of five weeks on the top of the chart, becoming the second biggest selling single of the year. It entered the top 10 also in Austria (5), Finland (3), France (4), West Germany (3), Iceland (9), Norway (5), and Switzerland (2). In the latter, it was held off reaching number-one by [[Koreana (band)|Koreana]]'s "[[Hand in Hand (Olympic theme song)|Hand In Hand]]". On the [[Eurochart Hot 100]], the song hit number one in September 1988.<ref name="eurocharthot100"/> Outside Europe, "The Only Way Is Up" hit number-one in New Zealand, while reaching number two in Australia and Israel.<ref name="israel">{{cite web|url=https://israelcharts.com/|title=Israeli Charts|date=September 25, 1988|access-date=August 19, 2026|archive-date=June 26, 2026|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20260626205604/https://israelcharts.com/|url-status=live}} Search "The Only Way Is Up" for Israeli chart history.</ref> On the ''[[Billboard (magazine)|Billboard]]'' [[Hot Dance Club Play]] chart in the United States, it peaked at number two. 

"The Only Way Is Up" earned a [[Music recording certification|gold record]] in Australia and the UK, with a sale of 50,000 and 400,000 singles. And in France, it earned a [[Music recording certification|silver record]], after 200,000 units were sold there.
sections.text:
Yazz' cover of "The Only Way Is Up" was very successful globally. In Europe, it peaked at number-one in Belgium, Denmark, Ireland, Luxembourg, the Netherlands, Sweden
and the United Kingdom. In the last of these, it hit the top spot in its third week at the UK Singles Chart, on July 31, 1988. The single spent a total of five weeks on the top of the chart, becoming the second biggest selling single of the year. It entered the top 10 also in Austria (5), Finland (3), France (4), West Germany (3), Iceland (9), Norway (5), and Switzerland (2). In the latter, it was held off reaching number-one by Koreana's "Hand In Hand". On the Eurochart Hot 100, the song hit number one in September 1988. Outside Europe, "The Only Way Is Up" hit number-one in New Zealand, while reaching number two in Australia and Israel. On the Billboard Hot Dance Club Play chart in the United States, it peaked at number two. 

"The Only Way Is Up" earned a gold record in Australia and the UK, with a sale of 50,000 and 400,000 singles. And in France, it earned a silver record, after 200,000 units were sold there.

sections.wikitext: A music video was produced to promote the single.
